summary: Typing fast in the title row's search lost keys: "invoice" typed at a keyboard's speed came out "invie" or "invoie", and the list searched the wrong words. The field showed the page's query, which comes back through the title slot a render later, so an older value landing after a newer key put the field back.
fix: The field keeps its own draft; the page's query only replaces it when it is something the field didn't send in the last 2 s (a page that clears or changes it). Test: titleRow.test.tsx "typed fast, every key stays".

summary: "/" from the list did nothing in the shell: it looked for a search inside the Library, but the search is the title row's, outside it. ⌘F worked; from the first row the search is 5 Shift+Tabs back (22 Tabs from the panel).
fix: In the title row "/" runs Edit › Find… (edit.find) as ⌘F does. Test: titleSearchApp.test.tsx "/ from a row of the list goes to the title row's search".

summary: ↓ and ↑ on a row of the list did nothing (only J and K moved between rows), so a person walking the list with arrows, as everywhere else, got stuck on the first row.
fix: ↓ ↑ on a row move from row to row as J K do, stop at the ends, and scroll the row into view; Shift+arrows and arrows off a row are left alone. Test: selection.test.tsx "↓ and ↑ on a row move between rows".

summary: With a non-Latin keyboard layout on (Urdu, the people this app is for), the app's keys didn't answer: the Library's F, J, K, X and / (where the layout moves it), and ⌘F, ⌘A, ⌘1…⌘6, ⌘[ ] and the menus' shortcuts, since they compared the typed character (e.key), then an Urdu letter. Arrows, Enter and Esc worked, so nothing was unreachable, only slower. The web's library-keys-core.cjs reads e.key the same way.
location: desktop/src/v2/actions/latinKey.ts; desktop/src/v2/library/LibraryV2.tsx (keys); desktop/src/v2/shell/NavShell.tsx (keys); desktop/src/v2/actions/registry.ts matchesShortcut; desktop/src/v2/actions/contextMenus.ts keyMatches; web/resources/js/library-keys-core.cjs
fix: latinKey(): when e.key isn't a character a US keyboard types, the key's place (e.code: KeyJ, Digit1, Slash, BracketLeft) stands for it; a Latin layout keeps its own letters (AZERTY). Used by the Library's and the shell's keys and both shortcut matchers. Tests: latinKey.test.ts, selection.test.tsx "on an Urdu keyboard layout…", navShell.test.tsx "on an Urdu keyboard layout…"; scripts/keyboardLibrary.mjs sends an Urdu layout's J, K, / and ⌘F/Ctrl+F. On a device: Windows checklist item 22, and a Mac with the Urdu layout.

screen: Every Urdu sentence with a value in it (a name, a title, a number)
summary: isolate() put each value in an isolate (FSI … PDI) and dropped a stray PDI, but an isolate the value opened itself and left open (a name typed with an FSI inside: "Ali" U+2068 "evil") was closed by the final PDI, so this isolate stayed open and the rest of the sentence after the value was inside it, its words in the wrong order. Only with v21_urdu.
fix: isolate() closes every isolate the value leaves open (one PDI per FSI, LRI or RLI still open) before the final PDI, which then also closes any override the value opened (U+202E). The same on the web (IsolatingTranslator) and the phone (EL-Fix). Test: src/i18n/i18n.test.tsx "the isolates are U+2068 and U+2069…" ("Ali" U+2068 "evil"; "Ali" U+202E U+2066 "x"; every value balanced).

screen: A row's lines, a toast, a dialog's description (every screen, in Urdu)
summary: The browsers' dir="auto" reads the first letter even inside an isolate, so an Urdu line that starts with a Latin name (t() puts the name in an FSI ... PDI isolate: "Imran کی بھیجی ہوئی ریکارڈنگ") was laid out left to right, its words out of order. D2 put a right-to-left mark (U+200F) before its own lines to work around it.
